_meta.description: enemy spawn group id -> how often its enemies rolled each SET of loot tables, observed on retail
_meta.authoritative: every set here is the lootTableLoot key set of one retail enemy result; nothing is interpolated
_meta.derivation: dungeonGeneratedDataList -> enemyGeneratedData keyed BY spawn group id -> lootTableLoot keys
_meta.whyASetDistribution: the table set is a property of the enemy, not always of the group. 1062 of 1066 groups always produced the same set, but the 4 that vary hold more than half of all enemy results -- they are the groups that spawn a mix of enemy types. Keying a group to one fixed set would give every enemy in those groups the commonest type's loot.
_meta.howToDraw: look the spawn group up, draw one SET weighted by n, then roll each table in it against enemy_loot.json at the enemy's level. A group absent from this file was never observed: the consumer decides the fallback, and must say which it used.
_meta.emptySetIsReal: an enemy that rolled no loot table at all is an observed outcome and is kept
_meta.deduplication: on (questId, sha1 of the dungeon entry), same as enemy_loot.json
